### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-messaging`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c1e6cf75a757a7e9102bae608ddb020135619882`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 41 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c1e6cf75a757a7e9102bae608ddb020135619882` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `43080ba718e315f55dca44f592bd88cb92558dd3` — the merge of head `6bd074ceffaca9a695f39b7934767e5fd51263e3` into base `c1e6cf75a757a7e9102bae608ddb020135619882`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 43080ba718e315f55dca44f592bd88cb92558dd3 && git checkout 43080ba718e315f55dca44f592bd88cb92558dd3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c1e6cf75a757a7e9102bae608ddb020135619882 6bd074ceffaca9a695f39b7934767e5fd51263e3 && git checkout -B drift-repro c1e6cf75a757a7e9102bae608ddb020135619882 && git merge --no-ff 6bd074ceffaca9a695f39b7934767e5fd51263e3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c1e6cf75a757a7e9102bae608ddb020135619882
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c1e6cf75a757a7e9102bae608ddb020135619882` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

- **Card fit (#36369 S1):** `readSnapshot` pages `digest = 'none'` by id cursor (`id > last`, `orderBy id asc`) before the `sys_migration` claim; the rewrite loop iterates that snapshot once with the same compare-and-set (`where: { id, digest: 'none' }`, row's own organization). The post-batch re-read and its `seen` set are gone, so a `none` written during the pass is never read. A failure on any snapshot page answers `read-failed` before the claim (nothing recorded, next boot retries). Matches ruling 7073270426 item 4.
- **Pins and ablations:** "a none written during the pass is not rewritten" (new explicit `none` row and a `daily` row switched to `none` survive; `converted: 1`), multi-page snapshot (`pageSize: 2`, 5 rows, 2 orgs), claim fails after the read, another node claims first. Ablation 1 (re-read restored) turned the first pin red (expected 1, received 3); ablation 2 (one page only) turned the paging pin red (expected 5, received 2); both restored to HEAD.
- **Shape:** `Fixes #36369`, changeset for `@objectstack/service-messaging`, `Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none` (`l1-face.mjs --pr 36694` CLEAN). The new `PreferenceDigestConversionOptions` is module-exported only; seat read `src/index.ts` at this head: no export of `preference-digest-conversion`, so `no` holds. Changeset read sentence by sentence; it matches the diff.
- **Gates:** 37 success · 16 expected skip · 0 failed · 0 pending at 6bd074ce (Test Core 10/10 went green on its one rerun; the failing case on attempt 1 was the plugin-auth forced-reset OAuth test tracked on #36361, outside this diff).
- **Accepted deviation, stated in the body:** a claim that fails leaves the next boot to take a new snapshot, so a `none` written between those two boots is converted. Nothing can record the earlier snapshot when the ledger write itself failed; the failure is logged at `error` naming the fix. The card's "also covers" sentence is read as covering the within-boot case only, which is pinned.
- **Optional items, split off (card's done-when allows it):** (1) the Notification Settings page has no "follow the organization again" action for digest or quiet hours; (2) `QUIET_HOURS_OFF` is spelled in `preference-resolver.ts` and the UI `myPreferences.ts` with no pin tying them. Both go to triage as follow-up filings on #32588; neither is done here.
- **Landing:** `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 36694`: NOT governed, +190/-61. `landing-k.mjs`: K = 5. Tier S: ready + auto-merge by the seat.
